# **Daily UPI Settlement Reconciliation With Sales and Bank Statements**


*UPI has turned into one of the most used payment methods for Indian businesses, like seriously everyone’s using it now. From small retail stores and restaurants to wholesalers, service providers, and even online sellers, businesses can get dozens, or sometimes hundreds, of UPI payments daily. And while UPI helps collections move faster, the annoying part is reconciling it all with sales records and bank statements when the transaction volume keeps climbing.*


Doing daily settlement reconciliation basically helps businesses confirm that the amount they counted as sales is the same amount that landed in the bank account. It also makes it easier to spot missing payments, duplicate entries, settlement gaps, refunds, and those little transaction charges. If you have the right billing and accounting workflow, this can become more accurate and way less time-consuming too. In this guide, we will learn how to do ***daily UPI settlement reconciliation with sales and bank statements*** .


## **What is UPI Reconciliation?**


UPI settlement reconciliation is basically the task of comparing UPI payment records against sales invoices, payment recipients, and the entries from bank statements. The main goal is to check that every UPI collection noted a sale has been properly settled into the business bank account.


For example, imagine a customer buys goods worth 2500 and pays ****[UPI](https://www.npci.org.in/product/ecosystem-statistics/upi) ; the sale should show 2500, the matching UPI transaction should indicate a successful payment, and later the bank statement should show duplicate entries, settlement gaps, refunds, and those little transaction charges. If you have the right billing and accounting workflow, this can become more accurate and way less time-consuming too.


This reconciliation became especially important if the business is using more than one UPI ID, QR codes, payment gateways, or collection accounts.


## **Why Daily Reconciliation Matters**


If you wait till the end of the month to reconcile UPI activity, then even small discrepancies can get hard to trace, because the details are already buried in a pile. A daily reconciliation approach helps businesses catch issues while transaction information is still fresh and easier to access.


For instance, if payment is shown as successful but it doesn't show up in the bank statement, the business can investigate right away. Similarly, if there’s an unexpected bank credit, it can be cross-checked against that day’s sales and UPI transaction records.


Daily reconciliation also boosts cash flow visibility. Business owners can quickly investigate right away. Similarly, if there is an unexpected bank credit, it can be cross-checked against that day’s sales and UPI transaction records.


Daily reconciliation also boosts cash flow visibility. Business owners can quickly understand what money was really collected, instead of only trusting the sales number shown in the billing system.


## **The Three Records You Need to Match**


A solid UPI reconciliation process usually relies on three things: sales records, UPI transaction records and bank statements. The sales record includes items like invoice number, customer details, invoice amount, payment mode, and any transaction reference that’s available.


The UPI record includes the transaction date, transaction ID or UTR, amount, status and settlement information. The bank statement gives the final confirmation that the funds actually reached the business bank account. It may include settlement references, narration, and the credited amount.


These should be matched using transaction references, dates, amounts, and settlement details, rather than just relying on the customer name, because that’s not reliable enough in practice.


## **How Daily UPI Reconciliation Works**


First, collect all of the day’s sales and payment records. Businesses should locate every invoice where UPI was chosen, then compare those invoices with the corresponding UPI transactions. Next, confirm which transactions are truly successful. A transaction that is marked pending, failed, or reversed should not be treated as a completed collection automatically.


After that, compare the successful UPI transaction with the bank statement. The bank statement received by the bank should align with the relevant settlement amount. If a payment gateway or intermediary sits between the business and the bank, the settlement might come through as sales and payment records to the consolidated settlement, rather than assuming the bank will show ten separate credited lines.


## **Creating a Daily UPI Reconciliation Routine**


You want a consistent reconciliation time each day, not whenever someone remembers At the end of the day, the accounts person should review UPI sales, successful payment entries, pending ones, refunds, and bank credits too.


If anything doesn't match, don't ignore it. Put it on an exception list first. Then the reason can be checked later, once the next settlement report or bank statement is available. Even this small routine can significantly reduce month-end stress and provide much better clarity on day-to-day collections.


## **What Should Be Done When the Amount Does Not Match?**


If the UPI total and the bank settlement do not align, the first thing is to confirm the[settlement is for the same state](https://getswipe.in/blog/article/daily-cash-card-upi-closing-checklist-retail-shops) . After that, check whether there are pending transactions, refund reversals, duplicate payments, consolidated settlements, or some adjustment from the payment processing side.


Also verify the transaction reference against the UPI provider and the bank statement. If the gap still can’t be explained, keep the supporting transaction records on file until the matter is sorted out.


## **Conclusion**


UPI reconciliation should not be treated as only a month-end chore. Doing it daily gives business read collection and helps stop small differences from becoming hard-to-trace accounting issues.


By matching sales records with UPI transactions and[bank statements every day](https://getswipe.in/blog/article/payment-gateway-settlements) , businesses can keep cleaner books, spot payment problems sooner, and improve confidence in the cash-flow records. And when billing software supports payment tracking plus reporting, the whole thing gets faster, more systematic, and easier to manage even when transaction volume keeps climbing.


## **FAQS**


### **What is UPI settlement reconciliation?**


UPI settlement reconciliation is the matching of UPI payment transactions with sales invoices and bank statement credits to confirm recorded collections actually arrived.


### **Why should UPI Payments be reconciled daily?**


Reconciling daily helps catch failed payments, missing settlements, duplicate records, refunds, reversals, and entry mistakes while the data is still relatively easy to verify.


### **What is a UTR number in UPI reconciliation?**


A UTR, or Unique Transaction Reference, is a transaction reference number that helps identify and trace a specific payment when comparing UPI records with bank statements.


### **Can the UPI payment date and bank statement date be different?**


Yes. A successful UPI transaction might be credited to the business bank account later. So reconciliation should consider both the transaction date and the settlement date.


### **What if a UPI payment is missing from the bank statement?**


First, check whether the payment is still pending settlement or whether it got included in a consolidated settlement. Then use the transaction reference and UPI provider records for additional verification.
